title: Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC
supports: D2W hybrid bonder accuracy 100 nm @ 3 sigma (alignment, worst corner, glass-on-glass), up to 2,000 CPH dry cycle (via search snippet; resp-cell-wafer-foundry WebSearch 1/3). Used for RT-PROC-cell-wafer-foundry-01: D2W placement fits the 0.375 um overlay budget at 1.5 um pitch with ~3.7x margin

title: Applied and Besi unveil integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonder
supports: Applied/Besi Kinex integrated D2W hybrid bonder (surface prep, bond, metrology in one tool); Applied: 'We have to achieve 100-nm alignment, at three sigma'; in use at multiple logic, memory and OSAT customers (via search snippet; resp-cell-wafer-foundry WebSearch 1/3)

title: Applied Materials and BESI Launch High-Volume Die-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding Platform
supports: Next-generation D2W hybrid bonder targeted for 2026 launch at 50 nm accuracy or better; following generation aims <25 nm (via search snippet; roadmap claim, not a shipped-tool measurement; resp-cell-wafer-foundry WebSearch 1/3)

title: 2026 IEEE ECTC to showcase the latest electronic packaging technologies
supports: ECTC 2026 ASML paper: D2W bonding overlay feasible through improved die placement accuracy and symmetric magnification (Ms) correction (via search snippet; resp-cell-wafer-foundry WebSearch 1/3)

title: ALD Al2O3 as a hydrogen barrier for a-IGZO TFT stability (Ajou University repository)
supports: Under hydrogen exposure an H2O-ALD-Al2O3-passivated a-IGZO TFT shifted Vth ~-12 V; an O3-ALD-Al2O3 passivated device shifted only ~-0.66 V (H trapped by C-O bonds); bilayer H2O/O3 Al2O3 used (via search snippet; resp-cell-wafer-foundry WebSearch 2/3). Used for RT-DEV-cell-wafer-foundry-01: one barrier gives ~18x, not the >=1e3 the bond-plane inventory needs, so barrier stack + standoff + measurement gate

title: KAIST SSMD: thin ALD Al2O3 under PECVD SiNx passivation for IGZO TFTs
supports: IGZO TFT with thin ALD Al2O3 under PECVD SiNx showed no significant negative turn-on shift after passivation; PECVD SiNx is itself a hydrogen source (via search snippet; resp-cell-wafer-foundry WebSearch 2/3)

title: Hydrogen in oxide-semiconductor TFTs (J. Mater. Chem. C 2025, open access)
supports: Hydrogen incorporated during SiNx deposition degrades oxide-channel stability and uniformity, especially for high-mobility channels; hydrogen can act as a shallow donor or passivate defects depending on excess oxygen (via search snippet; resp-cell-wafer-foundry WebSearch 2/3)
